literal: Deity not-worshipping, husband having-worshipped she-who-rises, 'pour' upon-saying, will-pour rain.
translation: If a wife who does not worship any other deity rises worshipping her husband, the rain will pour down at her command.
modern: தெய்வத்தை வணங்காமல், தன் கணவனையே வணங்கித் துயில் எழுகின்ற பெண், 'மழை பெய்' என்று சொன்னால் உடனே மழை பெய்யும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the immense power of a wife's devotion and moral strength. The poet states that a woman who does not worship any external deity, but instead rises each day worshipping her husband, possesses such spiritual power that even nature obeys her. If she commands the rain to fall, it will immediately pour down. The key words 'தொழாஅள்' (she who does not worship other gods) and 'தொழுதெழுவாள்' (she who rises worshipping her husband) contrast the redirection of her devotion, while 'பெய்யெனப் பெய்யும்' (will pour as soon as told to pour) illustrates the absolute authority her virtue commands over the elements.
